_: Standing ad SFX palette. Ratified by ear 2026-09-03. Read this file before adding SFX to an ad; do not re-generate a class that is already here. NEVER use tick sounds (class rejected 2026-09-17, files deleted 2026-09-18). The audio files are local-only (gitignored, ElevenLabs terms).
ratifiedBy: Umair — ear QC, in context, on real cuts (not bare snippets)
scope: ad-style / editorial films. Tutorials and shorts inherit it only where an ad-energy accent is wanted.

provenance.note: The original ElevenLabs one-shots plus generate-palette.mjs, the prompts that made them. Kept intact as the record; this folder is the working home.

measurement.onset: node tools/sfx/onset.mjs tools/sfx/palette   (first sample > 5% of the file's own peak, 30fps frame budget)
measurement.peak: ffmpeg -i <f> -af volumedetect -f null -   (max_volume; rulebook rfe 37 — volumedetect, not astats)

mixLadder._: Measured from the reel's ratified gains (sourcePeak + clipGain). Two tiers, ~6 dB apart. Reproduce the LADDER, not the gain numbers — gains never port between films (rulebook rfv 29); re-measure with normalize.mjs every time.
mixLadder.currency_ticks_dB: REJECTED CLASS as of 2026-09-17 — the tick tier no longer exists; accents only.

tick-a.deleted: 2026-09-18 — file removed from repo and disk on Umair's order; tick is a rejected class (2026-09-17). NEVER use tick sounds. Kept below as the record only.
tick-a.useWhen: The default tick. Grid currency — a row completing, a soft/locked crossfade cut, a cursor press frame. The most-placed of the three (4 of 17 reel cues).
reelCues: 9.80 cut 3 locked crossfade (soft cut, soft cue)
tick-a.REJECTED: Class rejected by Umair 2026-09-17 — never place, never regenerate.

tick-b.deleted: 2026-09-18 — file removed from repo and disk on Umair's order; tick is a rejected class (2026-09-17). NEVER use tick sounds. Kept below as the record only.
tick-b.useWhen: Brighter tick. Second in a rotation, or the tick that starts a run (an odometer roll, a chip appearing).
tick-b.REJECTED: Class rejected by Umair 2026-09-17 — never place, never regenerate.

tick-c.deleted: 2026-09-18 — file removed from repo and disk on Umair's order; tick is a rejected class (2026-09-17). NEVER use tick sounds. Kept below as the record only.
tick-c.onsetVerdict: LATE at 30fps — compensate at PLACEMENT (cue 30ms early), do NOT re-trim
tick-c.useWhen: Warmest/woodiest tick. Third in a rotation — the hot-swap, the last row, a tile popping.
tick-c.warning: This file sits at the mp3 encoder priming floor (~20-30ms, rulebook rfw 24 / rfe 26) — re-encodes do not converge. The reel shipped a re-trimmed copy at -ss 0.029: its onset reads 21ms but its peak collapsed to -15.1 dB, because the trim cut past the transient. Onset is measured relative to the file's OWN peak, so destroying the transient FLATTERS the onset number. The palette keeps the un-trimmed original (-0.3 dB) and compensates at placement — the reel's t values ending .579/.479/.379 are exactly that compensation.
tick-c.REJECTED: Class rejected by Umair 2026-09-17 — never place, never regenerate.

impact-a.useWhen: Hard cut. The throw/whip that lands a new scene. Cleanest of the three impacts.
impact-a.warning: Quiet source (-23.1). Needs ~+15 dB. This is the regen of a near-silent v1 (impact-a-v1-near-silent.mp3 is kept in the candidates folder as the failed roll).

impact-b.useWhen: Hard cut, snappier/drier than impact-a. Use as the second impact so consecutive cuts do not read as one sample.
impact-b.warning: UNDER the -25 dB near-silence flag (rulebook rfv 28). Carries a +20 dB compensating gain, so it raises its own noise floor. Re-roll it when a generation budget exists; approved by ear at reel level, not certified clean.

impact-c.useWhen: Impact for a settle, not a cut — a counter landing, a value resolving.
impact-c.warning: UNDER the -25 dB near-silence flag (rulebook rfv 28). Carries a +19 dB compensating gain. Same re-roll note as impact-b.

boom-a.useWhen: Film OPEN, and any overshoot/pulse that wants weight without a cut under it. Rounded attack — it swells rather than snaps.

boom-b.useWhen: Film CLOSE, and big landings — a zoom-through arriving, a scene receding into the lockup. Longest tail in the palette (1.48s); do not place one inside another's decay.

rejected._: REJECTED BY EAR 2026-09-03. Files stay on disk in tools/sfx/palette-candidates-2026-09-03/ as rejected candidates. Never auto-select, never regenerate, never re-place. Consistent with the standing 2026-06-10 ad-sound ruling: punchy-clean, no cinematic whoosh/sparkle cheese.
rejected.verdict: Umair, 2026-09-03: "Fuck this SFX, specially the shimmer and swish woosh sounds."
rejected.consequence: All 6 of their clips were unmapped from the reel and the 4 sounds dropped from its library. The cuts they covered keep their tick/impact/boom cues; the sheen moments and the invisible cursor-continuity cut get nothing — the bed carries them.
